title: fix(metadata-protocol): tier 3 refuses to unregister an object bound to an installed package (#7012)
body:
Fixes #7012

Ships **option C** of the maintainer ruling of 2026-08-09 on #6853 — the stop-the-bleed half, ahead of direction B's ADR work. Nothing here re-litigates the accepted cost, and nothing here implements B.

## The outage, reproduced before writing a line of the fix

Measured on this branch's base (`2f3e79351`) with a throwaway probe on the `protocol-delete-object-registry-heal.test.ts` harness shape — real `SchemaRegistry` + real `SysMetadataRepository` over an in-memory engine — on a **tenant kernel, no escape hatch, no operator action**:

```json
{"loadMetaFromDb":{"loaded":1,"errors":0,"invalid":0,"storeUnavailable":false},
 "afterHydration_isArtifactBacked":false,
 "insertBeforeDelete_ok":true,
 "deleteReceipt":{"success":true,"reset":true,
                  "message":"Deleted object 'myapp_invoice' — it no longer exists. [seq=1]"},
 "storedRowsAfter":0,
 "objectContributorsAfter":0,
 "getObjectAfter":null,
 "dataCrudAfter":{"code":"OBJECT_NOT_FOUND","status":404,"object":"myapp_invoice"},
 "dataRows":1}
```

`dataRows: 1` is the point — the table still holds the row the object can no longer reach.

The probe needs no hatch because it uses the real boot order across two sessions: session 1 persists the overlay while nothing ships the name (so the two-tier gate has nothing to refuse), session 2 installs the package, registers the packaged object, then hydrates. That is #6853 P6 exactly.

## Mechanism

`SchemaRegistry.registerObject` **splices out** the same-package `own` contributor before pushing the new one, so an overlay row whose `package_id` equals the packaged owner's id **destroys** the packaged definition at write time — it is not shadowed, and no second copy exists anywhere in the registry. `loadMetaFromDb` replays that replacement on every boot with no authorization gate and no log, stamping `_provenance: 'org'` server-side (deliberately, cloud#970).

`getArtifactItem` for an `object` is exactly `_provenance !== 'org'`, so `isArtifactBacked` — the predicate tier 3's "AND IT NEVER RETIRES A CODE-SHIPPED OBJECT" guard reads — is **the one predicate the overwrite falsified**, and it answers `false` for an object the package still ships.

## The predicate chosen, and why

Tier 3 now also refuses when the owner contributor's package binding names a **currently-installed** package:

```
registry.getObjectOwner(name)?.packageId   ->  registry.getPackage(packageId)
```

- The **binding** is trustworthy where the definition is not: the replacement rule fires only when the two package ids **match**, so the surviving contributor provably carries the packaged owner's id — the one fact the overwrite cannot change, because it is the overwrite's own precondition.
- **"Installed" is a fact about the process, not about the destroyed body.** `ObjectQL.registerApp` calls `SchemaRegistry.installPackage(manifest)` immediately before registering the manifest's objects (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`), durable `sys_packages` records are re-installed at boot by `service-package`, and `registerPlugin` objects are keyed to the **parent** package, which `registerApp` installed. So a package-shipped object always has a record.
- The `'sys_metadata'` sentinel is handled **by construction**, not by a special case: nothing installs a package under it.

Two things the predicate deliberately does **not** ask, each pinned by a test:

- **not `enabled` / `status`** — `disablePackage` flips lifecycle flags and removes no contributor, so a disabled package's objects stay registered and stay dispatchable; reading the flag would unregister a definition nothing else removes, which is the same outage through a second door.
- **not the manifest's `objects` list** — that re-asks "is this code-shipped", the question whose answer was destroyed, and it is absent for `registerPlugin`-contributed objects.

Note on the dispatch's assumption 2: `registry.getPackage(pkgId)` returning `null` in #6853's measurement was a fact about **that probe** (it called `registerObject` directly, installing nothing), not about installed packages. The two questions are different and the installed-package one is answerable here.

The refusal is **stated in the log**, not swallowed — the same discipline the ADR-0029 extender refusal one line up already carries: a runtime that disagrees with `sys_metadata` must be visible rather than inferred later.

## Accepted cost (ruled — recorded, not re-argued)

A package-bound **runtime-authored** object (Studio package workspace, #4636) carries a real `package_id` too, so it is indistinguishable from a package-shipped one by binding alone: some genuinely deleted objects stay registered until restart — listable, and rowless. Per this walk's own REGISTER WIDE / RETIRE NARROW argument that is the cheap direction; a surplus entry degrades to "listable but rowless" and the next reload heals it, a wrongly retired one 404s data CRUD for every tenant. The honest fix for the distinguishability itself is #6853's direction B.

## File surface — every file, and the declared deviations

| File | Why |
|---|---|
| `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` | tier 3 of `restoreArtifactRegistryView` (the decision), plus one new **private** helper `installedPackageBindingForObject` carrying the argument |
| `packages/objectql/src/protocol-delete-object-package-binding-guard.test.ts` | the regression pin, both directions |
| `.changeset/lucky-buttons-shave.md` | user-visible fix |

**Deviations from the declared surface, stated file by file:**

1. The helper is a **second symbol** in `protocol.ts` rather than an inline expression in tier 3. It reads no new state and changes no other call site; it exists so the argument (why `isArtifactBacked` cannot be trusted at this point, what the predicate does and does not ask, and the ruled cost) lives next to the code instead of in a commit message. The decision itself is still one branch at one point.
2. **No new registry plumbing.** `getObjectOwner` and `getPackage` both already exist and `getPackage` is already declared in the engine contract, so `packages/spec` is untouched and no cross-seat declaration on #6298 is needed.
3. `packages/objectql` gains a test file only — no source change.

Untouched, as required: `saveMetaItem`'s two-tier write gate region (#6973 / `session_01LGRN2cSRfggfX9B2L83bQc`), `assertSortFieldsExist`, `packages/spec`, `content/docs/releases/`. Tiers 1 and 2 are unchanged — verified rather than assumed: both conclude a lower layer still serves the name, so neither ever reaches a removal, and the damage is entirely tier 3 deciding *to remove*.

## Reverse verification — direction predicted before running

Predicted **RED**, and only on the positive-direction cases. Fix taken out with `git checkout 2f3e79351 -- packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` (this branch's own base, never a moving `origin/main`), `metadata-protocol` rebuilt, pins re-run.

| Case | Predicted | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| package-bound object survives the delete | red | **red** — `expected undefined to be defined` at `:308` |
| DISABLED installed package still protects | red | **red** at `:412` |
| plural `objects` spelling guarded | red | **red** at `:432` |
| control-plane kernel guarded | red | **red** at `:452` |
| boot replay destroys the definition, binding survives | green both ways | **green** — a guard on the premise, not evidence |
| package-LESS runtime object still retired | green both ways | **green** — a guard against over-refusal |
| binding naming a NON-installed package still retired | green both ways | **green** — a guard; it is also why every pre-existing pin in `protocol-delete-object-registry-heal.test.ts` stays green |

`Tests 4 failed | 3 passed (7)` with the fix out; `Tests 7 passed (7)` with it in.

**One prediction went unmeasured in the reverse direction and is not counted as passed:** the "survives" case fails at its first post-delete assertion, so its data-plane recovery and warning-text assertions never execute with the fix out. They are measured green in the fixed direction, and the pre-fix data-plane verdict was measured separately by the throwaway probe quoted above (`OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` / 404) rather than inferred.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol test` — `Test Files 65 passed (65)`, `Tests 827 passed (827)`
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql test` — `Test Files 163 passed (163)`, `Tests 2793 passed (2793)`
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime test` — `Test Files 117 passed (117)`, `Tests 1761 passed (1761)` (run as the downstream consumer of the heal; its first run's 91 collect failures were the fresh-worktree stale-artefact trap, gone after `--filter '@objectstack/runtime^...' build`)
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck` — `Done`
- `metadata-protocol` has no `typecheck` script (measured DEBT entry of 63): `tsc --noEmit` counts **63**, exactly the ledger's number, so `check:type-check-debt` is unmoved
- gates: `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:route-envelope`, `check:meta-type-normalized`, `check:empty-changeset`, `check:adr-anchors`, `check:wildcard-fallthrough` — all PASS; `node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs` OK; `eslint --no-inline-config` clean on both changed files
